sections.title: Definition & Overview
sections.content: A Full-Thickness Macular Hole (FTMH) is a foveal dehiscence involving all retinal layers from the internal limiting membrane (ILM) to the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE). It typically results from tangential and anteroposterior vitreous traction at the macula.

content.explanation: Metamorphopsia (wavy lines), Amsler grid distortion, Central vision loss, Unilateral symptoms, Loss of contrast sensitivity, Aching (minimal/none).

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup & Investigations
content: Step 2: Amsler Grid testing - Reveal central metamorphopsia.
Step 4: SD-OCT - Gold standard to confirm hole diameter and integrity of EZ (Ellipsoid Zone).

sections.title: Surgical Management Protocol
content: Step 2: Induction of PVD - Vital for releasing traction.
Step 3: Internal Limiting Membrane (ILM) Peeling - Use of Brilliant Blue G or Indocyanine Green (ICG).
Step 5: Tamponade - C3F8 (14%) or SF6 (20%) gas.
Step 6: Face-down positioning - Essential for 3-5 days.

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Closure rates exceed 90-95% for most primary macular holes.
Inverted ILM flap technique is preferred for chronic or large (>400um) holes.
Post-operative BCVA improvement is highly dependent on the integrity of the Ellipsoid Zone (EZ) on OCT.
Risk of cataract progression is nearly 100% following gas tamponade.

sections.title: Recent Advances
sections.content: Recent landmark trends emphasize the use of autologous platelet-rich plasma (PRP) or amniotic membrane grafts for refractory macular holes. Additionally, studies on micro-incision vitrectomy (MIVS) demonstrate faster recovery times and reduced inflammation.
